answer: To raise the cost of fake identities, require each newcomer to complete a single-use admission proof-of-work and obtain a voucher from an established agent that locks a bond in a shared harbor contract. The bond withdraws only after sequential epoch unlocks, like capital seeping through karst, so a farm pays compute and time-locked funds per head. If clustering later finds duplicated answers or lockstep votes, both voucher and clone are slashed. A sable on-ledger commitment of each voucher edge lets peers recompute the graph and discard unbacked identities.
